phase3_findings.description: Restart guidance claims a query reaching a renamed or dropped table is refused before it runs; check_catalog runs once at startup and the guard checks only rule-set file names, so such queries reach MySQL and fail with its own unknown-table error naming the table.
check_catalog docstring omits that parent_rule compare columns are type-checked on parent_table.

parent_rule refusal message derives allowed kinds from model_fields['kind'].annotation.__args__[0]; an annotation shape change would raise AttributeError/IndexError instead of a path-naming ValueError.

## Verdict: REJECT (a checklist FAIL and an Important documentation falsehood, both in docs/external/rule-sets.md)
This PR is not ready to merge. The new operator docs contain a TOML example that does not load, and a restart note that claims a refusal the code never makes.
Rule applied: rule 1 — a checklist FAIL at or above the threshold → REJECT

## Code Review Findings

### 🟠 Important / Major
1. docs/external/rule-sets.md line 197 says that, until a restart, "a query that reaches a renamed or dropped table is refused before it runs". Nothing does this. `check_catalog` runs only once, at startup (`preflight.py` and `rule_sets.py`). The guard checks table names against the rule-set file, not against the live catalog. So a query against a renamed or dropped table that is still listed, or a row-rule read of a dropped unlisted link table, reaches MySQL and fails with MySQL's own unknown-table error, which can name the table. This is the same pass-through the sentence describes for columns. (raised by 3/4 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=not-held; evidence: published operator doc sentence; making it true changes no output; git grep for rule-sets.md across .py/.sh/.yml/.jq found no reader -->
- VC-25: FAIL (important) — The external doc's TOML example loads: orders declares deleted_at as a predicate column, the inherit parent_rule compares region_id which customers must declare, and the products referenced_by uses an unlisted customer_products link. [docs/external/rule-sets.md] [behavior-inert prose cap] <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=not-held; evidence: first-conjunct=held (the TOML example in docs/external/rule-sets.md is prose no code path executes; making it valid TOML changes no program output or branch) limb-one=held (no .sh/.py/.yml consumer or agent-instruction file reads docs/external/rule-sets.md for behavior) limb-two=not-held (published operator documentation page) -->

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Semantic checks pass: orders declares deleted_at in predicate_columns (rule_sets.py _check_row_rules: column() uses columns+predicate_columns); the inherit parent_rule compare on region_id requires customers to declare region_id (rule_sets.py:441-442) and the doc says so at rule-sets.md:186; referenced_by with link.table customer_products unlisted is allowed (rule_sets.py:450-452, only checked when listed), source_table customers is listed and source_id_column id is declared; no cycle (products->customers, orders->customers). However the example does not load as written: load_rule_sets parses with tomllib.loads (rule_sets.py:805; Python >=3.11 per pyproject, TOML 1.0), and TOML 1.0 forbids newlines inside inline tables. docs/external/rule-sets.md:174-175 puts a newline inside the inline table after `parent_column = "id",` before `parent_rule = ...`, and lines 182-183 put a newline inside the products row_rule inline table after `source_id_column = "id",` before `link = ...`. tomllib's parse_inline_table only skips space/tab, so both raise TOMLDecodeError, which load_rule_sets reports as RuleSetFileError 'is not valid TOML'. Only multi-line arrays (as at lines 151-154) are legal. The claim that the example loads is false for the parent_rule and unlisted-link parts. I did not run the parser; this rests on reading the code and the TOML 1.0 rule.

  </details>

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (2)
<details><summary>2 items</summary>

1. In src/sqllens/rule_sets.py lines 1112-1117, the revised `check_catalog` docstring says every `compare` column's `DATA_TYPE` is checked. It does not say that `parent_rule` compares are type-checked on `parent_table`. The behavior is correct, since `_catalog_reads` adds those compares, but the summary is incomplete. (raised by 1/4 agents)
2. In src/sqllens/rule_sets.py, `RuleSet._check_row_rules` builds the `parent_rule` refusal message from `kind.model_fields["kind"].annotation.__args__[0]`. If that annotation's shape changes, this raises `AttributeError` or `IndexError` instead of a `ValueError` that names the record path. (raised by 1/4 agents)

</details>

- [ ] Loading refuses a null-test node, naming its record path, when at minimum: its column is not declared on its table; it has no `column`; it has any field besides `kind` and `column`.
- [ ] On MySQL, with no flat `[[rls]]` rules configured, a `query_database` request under a set whose `orders` rule is `is_null` on `deleted_at` returns every orders row whose `deleted_at` is NULL and no row whose `deleted_at` is not NULL; with `is_not_null` it returns the reverse.
